items.label: text
items.text: displacement reaction a chemical reaction in which a more reactive element replaces a less reactive one in its compound

items.label: text
items.text: displayed formula a formula that shows all the bonds in a molecule as individual lines. Each line represents a pair of shared electrons in a covalent bond

items.label: text
items.text: dot-and-cross diagram a representation of how electrons are arranged in ions or molecules

items.label: text
items.text: double bond atoms sharing two pairs of electrons in a covalent bond

items.label: text
items.text: drive off force something to go away

items.label: text
items.text: dry ice solid carbon dioxide

items.label: text
items.text: ductile a property of metal that allows it to be drawn out into wires

items.label: text
items.text: dynamic equilibrium equilibrium means the concentrations of the reactants and the products in a reversible reaction remain constant. Dynamic means the reactions are still continuing, but the rate of the forward reaction is equal to the rate of the reverse reaction

items.label: text
items.text: electrode a conductor through which electricity is passed into and out of an electrolyte

items.label: text
items.text: electrolysis the chemical change caused by passing an electric current through a compound that is either molten or in solution

items.label: text
items.text: electrolyte a liquid that undergoes electrolysis. Electrolytes are molten ionic compounds or solutions containing ions

items.label: text
items.text: electrolytic cella compartment in which electrolysis occurs

items.label: text
items.text: electron a subatomic particle found in shells (energy levels) outside the nucleus of an atom. It has a relative mass of 1/1836 and a relative charge of 1–. For a neutral atom, the number of electrons = the number of protons = the atomic number

items.label: text
items.text: electronic configuration how electrons are arranged in the shells (energy levels) in an atom

items.label: text
items.text: electrostatic attraction the force of attraction between something that is positive and something that is negative

items.label: text
items.text: element a substance that cannot be split into anything simpler by chemical means. An element contains atoms of the same atomic number

items.label: text
items.text: empirical formulagives the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms present in a compound. It can be worked out from experimental data

items.label: text
items.text: end point the point at which the indicator changes colour in a titration endothermic reactions in which heat energy is taken in from the surroundings energetics a study of energy change in chemical reactions enthalpy change the amount of heat energy taken in or given out in a chemical reaction. It has the symbol ∆H

items.label: text
items.text: enzymes biological catalysts, usually consisting of proteins

items.label: text
items.text: ester esters are organic compounds formed by the reaction of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid. Theyhave the functional group -COO-

items.label: text
items.text: esterificationa chemical reaction in which an alcohol and a carboxylic acid react together to form an ester

items.label: text
items.text: evaporation the change of state from a liquid to a vapour. It occurs at a temperature below the boiling point and only at the surface of the liquid

items.label: text
items.text: excess having more than enough of a reactant to react with all of something else

items.label: text
items.text: exothermic reactions in which heat energy is given out to the surroundings

items.label: text
items.text: fade lose colour and brightness

items.label: text
items.text: fermentation converting sugar such as glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide using enzymes in yeasts

items.label: text
items.text: filtratethe liquid that comes through the filter paper during filtration

items.label: text
items.text: filtration a process to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid

items.label: text
items.text: fizz make many bubbles, producing a continuous sound flake off come off in small pieces

items.label: text
items.text: flash shine suddenly and brightly for a short period of time

items.label: text
items.text: flush out force something out

items.label: text
items.text: formula a representation of a chemical showing the elements present

items.label: text
items.text: forward reaction from reactants to products (the leftto-right reaction)

items.label: text
items.text: fossil fuels these include coal, gas and fuels derived from crude oil, which all come from things that were once alive

items.label: text
items.text: fractional distillation a process to separate two liquids of similar boiling points, for example ethanol and water or the components of crude oil

items.label: text
items.text: fractionating column a piece of equipment used for separating vapours in fractional distillation

items.label: text
items.text: freezing the change of state from a liquid to a solid. It occurs at the freezing point
